rules.title: Rights During Arrest & Police Custody
rights_summary: Right to know the exact grounds of arrest immediately.
Right to inform a family member/friend as soon as detained.
Women cannot be arrested after sunset or before sunrise except in extraordinary circumstances with a female officer.
Right to consult a legal practitioner of choice and get a free medical checkup every 48 hours.
guidelines: Step 1: Ask the arresting officer for their name, ID tag, and an official Arrest Memo.
Step 2: Ensure an entry is made in the Police Station Diary (General Diary).
Step 3: Insist on contacting a family member or calling the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) for free lawyer support.
Step 4: Demand to be produced before a Judicial Magistrate within 24 hours of arrest.
rules.grievance_template:
To,
The Superintendent of Police / Judicial Magistrate,
Subject: Complaint Regarding Illegal Detention / Procedural Lapse During Arrest

I, {NAME}, hereby record that on {DATE}, I was detained/arrested at {WORKPLACE} without being provided grounds of arrest or an arrest memo.

I request immediate legal intervention and production before the Judicial Magistrate as per BNSS provisions.

rules.title: Protection Against Unfair Trade & Defective Goods
rights_summary: Right to protection against hazardous goods and unfair trade practices.
Right to full refund, replacement, or compensation for defective products or deficient services.
Protection against misleading advertisements and fake reviews.
guidelines: Step 1: Preserve tax invoice/receipt, product photographs, warranty cards, and order emails.
Step 2: Send a written notice/email to seller/company giving 7–14 days for resolution.
Step 3: Register a complaint on the National Consumer Helpline (NCH) at consumerhelpline.gov.in or call 1915.
Step 4: File an online e-Daakhil petition with the District Consumer Commission if unresolved.
rules.grievance_template:
To,
The Customer Care Manager / Seller,
Subject: Notice for Refund/Replacement of Defective Product

I, {NAME}, purchased {WORKPLACE} on {DATES} invoice no. {SURVEY_NO} for Rs. {AMOUNT}.

The product is defective/deficient. I request an immediate replacement or full refund within 7 days, failing which I will initiate e-Daakhil consumer court proceedings.

rules.title: Right to Timely Payment of Wages & Safe Work Conditions
governing_laws: Occupational Safety, Health & Working Conditions Code, 2020
rights_summary: Wages must be paid by the 7th or 10th of every calendar month.
Right to double wages for mandatory overtime work beyond legal hours.
Right to claim up to 10x compensation on unpaid wages.
guidelines: Step 1: Gather employment proof (Job Card, attendance logs, payment slips, or chat records).
Step 2: Send a written demand notice to your employer giving a 7-day resolution window.
Step 3: File an online grievance on the Shram Suvidha Portal or report to the District Labour Inspector.
Step 4: Approach the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) for free legal aid.
rules.grievance_template:
To,
The Labour Inspector / Employer,
Subject: Non-Payment of Pending Wages

I, {NAME}, was employed at {WORKPLACE}. My wages for {DATES} amounting to Rs. {AMOUNT} have not been released despite repeated demands.

Kindly release my payment within 7 days, failing which I will lodge a formal complaint under the Code on Wages.

rules.title: Protection Against Online Financial Fraud & Cyber Crimes
rights_summary: Right to report financial cyber fraud within the 'Golden Hour' (first 2 hours) to freeze stolen funds.
Protection against non-consensual publishing of personal photos or morphed images.
Right to privacy and data deletion for misuse of personal identifiers.
guidelines: Step 1: Immediately dial 1930 (National Cyber Crime Helpline) to lock fraudulent bank transfers.
Step 2: Take screenshots of payment receipts, fraud SMS/WhatsApp chats, and URLs.
Step 3: File a complaint on cybercrime.gov.in (can be filed anonymously for sexual/harassment content).
Step 4: Request bank to issue a lien on the fraud recipient account.
rules.grievance_template:
To,
The Cyber Crime Cell / Nodal Officer,
Subject: Reporting Online Financial Fraud / Cyber Harassment

I, {NAME}, report an unauthorized transaction of Rs. {AMOUNT} on {DATE} from my account.

Fraudulent Transaction Txn ID: {SURVEY_NO}. Kindly freeze the recipient account and initiate investigation under IT Act.

rules.title: Constitutional Guarantees & Enforcement of Remedies
rights_summary: Article 21: Right to Life & Personal Liberty (includes right to clean water, livelihood, and privacy).
Article 14 & 15: Prohibition of discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth.
Article 32: Right to move the High Court or Supreme Court directly via Writs for fundamental rights violation.
guidelines: Step 1: Document evidence showing state action or public authority violating fundamental rights.
Step 2: File a representation/appeal before the State Human Rights Commission (SHRC) or National Commission (NHRC).
Step 3: Approach the High Court under Article 226 by filing a Public Interest Litigation (PIL) or Writ Petition.
Step 4: Request free legal counsel from the High Court Legal Services Committee.
rules.grievance_template:
To,
The High Court Legal Services Committee / NHRC,
Subject: Representation Regarding Violation of Fundamental Right under Article 21/14

I, {NAME}, resident of {ADDRESS}, submit that public authorities at {VILLAGE} have arbitrarily deprived me/my community of fundamental entitlements.

I request legal representation to file a Writ Petition for enforcement of constitutional rights.

rules.title: Right to Information & Public Service Entitlements
rights_summary: Right to inspect government records, works, and obtain certified copies of government files.
Public Information Officer (PIO) must provide information within 30 days (48 hours if life/liberty is at stake).
Right to timely delivery of essential services (Ration, Birth Certificates, Caste Certificates).
guidelines: Step 1: Identify the relevant government department (e.g., Food & Civil Supplies, Panchayat).
Step 2: Draft a clear RTI application asking specific questions (avoid asking for opinions).
Step 3: Submit via rti-online portal or physically with a ₹10 court fee stamp (BPL cardholders are fee-exempt).
Step 4: File a First Appeal if no reply is received within 30 days.
rules.grievance_template:
To,
The Public Information Officer (PIO),
Office of {WORKPLACE},
Subject: Application under Section 6(1) of RTI Act, 2005

1. Name of Applicant: {NAME}
2. Information Sought: Please provide status report and certified copies regarding application no {SURVEY_NO} submitted on {DATE}.

Fee of Rs. 10 attached / Exempt under BPL category.

rules.title: Taxpayer Protections & Income Tax/GST Grievance Rights
rights_summary: Taxpayers' Charter: Right to fair, courteous, and prompt treatment by tax authorities.
Right to appeal against arbitrary tax demand notices within 30 days of service.
Right to receive income tax refund along with statutory interest on delayed refunds.
guidelines: Step 1: Check the authenticity of any tax notice on the e-filing portal using Document Identification Number (DIN).
Step 2: Do not share OTPs or bank details with callers claiming to be tax officers.
Step 3: File an online response or appeal via the e-Proceedings tab on incometax.gov.in.
Step 4: Submit a grievance on CPGRAMS or e-Nivaran if refund is delayed over 60 days.
rules.grievance_template:
To,
The Assessing Officer / Income Tax Ombudsman,
Subject: Application for Processing Pending Income Tax Refund

I, {NAME}, PAN: {SURVEY_NO}, filed my Income Tax Return for Assessment Year {DATES}.

My refund of Rs. {AMOUNT} remains unpaid. I request processing and release of refund along with interest under Section 244A.
